title: Positions the bot still holds after a failed sell are marked trades.status='failed', and every risk query counts only status='pending' buys, so stuck positions drop out of the open-position limit, the exposure cap and the daily-loss total and the bot keeps buying past its limits

evidence.note: still-held failed exit: updateTradeStatus.run('failed', ...) for operator visibility, then keepMonitoringFailedHeld (the position is kept and retried)
getDailyRealizedLoss counts only rows with a sell; a held, unsold position has no sell row, so its loss is not counted either
the restart scan already treats exit_status = 'exit_failed_held' as still open (UNION with pending); the risk queries do not

sibling_sites_checked: All five updateTradeStatus.run sites (git grep at the base SHA): bot.ts:1189 and :1514 (buy catch, AUD-BUY-002), bot.ts:1937 (restart: zero balance -> failed, correct), exitEngine.ts:668 (sold) and exitEngine.ts:1163 (still-held failed exit -> failed, this finding). All risk SQL in db.ts and riskManager.ts filters on status = 'pending'; none reads exit_state.exit_status. The restart-resume queries getResumeExitMonitorTrades / getResumeAntiRugTrades (db.ts:597-620) do include exit_failed_held.
severity_rationale: S1 OVERSPEND: more positions and more capital are put at risk than MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS and MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE allow whenever sells fail on held tokens, a common condition for sniped tokens (transfer tax, honeypot-like behaviour, liquidity pulled). Each stuck position frees one slot for a new buy. Bounded by the per-trade size and the wallet balance, so not S0.
recommendation: Count a position as open from its exit lifecycle (pending buy, or exit_state row present, including exit_failed_held) rather than from trades.status, in every risk query; keep the operator-visible 'failed' label separately. Card DB-01. Phase 24; nothing is changed in Phase 22.
